tested:
"catalyst8000v" (the spelled-out image name image-manager's own detector.py
recognizes as a DISTINCT alias from "cat8000v"/"c8000v" - see detector.py's
comment at ~line 476 explaining they're deliberately not merged there to avoid
a false match against "catalyst9000v"/cat9k) had NO key here, so an image
literally named "catalyst8000v" never matched the "cisco-cat8000v" key above:
get_profile()'s substring match needs "cat8000v" to appear in the normalized
image name, and "catalyst8000v" does not contain that substring ("catA-LYST"
breaks it up). Every catalyst8000v import silently fell through to
GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512MB/1cpu/qemu64), not this 4096MB/2cpu/host-passthrough
profile - live-confirmed 2026-07-18: GET /images showed
hardware_defaults={"cpu":1,"ram_mb":512,"profile_key":"generic:catalyst8000v"}
for the installed catalyst8000v image. Same bug class as the isrv fix below
(2026-07-12) - IOS-XE's first-boot crypto keygen + package extraction crash-loops
under 512MB, so the node never reaches RUNNING and the boot-wait times out.
Mirrors the csr1000v/cisco-csr1000vng duplicate-key pattern already used above.
